_doc: Every SFX type the acts may use. layer: foley (small object sounds, one per visible action), design (cinematic: builds, hits, transitions; few per act), bed (long, under a passage). anchor: what the event's t means - start (the sound starts at t), end (the sound ENDS at t: risers and swells land on the word), peak (its loudest point is at t: transitions and swooshes peak on the cut; pre = seconds of sound before the peak). d: default length in s (null = fixed length). level: peak dBFS at the mix input. Read by sfx.py (rendering, levels) and workflow/05-video/src/lib/cues.ts (anchors, thinning).

ruler_hiss.desc: a line drawn along a ruler

paper_slide.desc: a sheet or cut-out slid into place

card_slap.desc: a card or cut-out letter lands flat

tick.desc: a gear step, ruler tick, counter digit

click.desc: a cursor click, a part snapping in

sweep.desc: a scan line or a flood

shutter.desc: a camera shutter: a snapshot, a freeze-frame, a photo appears

notify.desc: a phone/app notification ding: an alert, a message, a margin call

glitch.desc: a digital stutter: a screen or chart breaking, a number corrupting

clock_tick.desc: a clock ticking (d seconds): time running out, a deadline

heartbeat.desc: one heartbeat (lub-dub): fear, a held breath

riser.desc: a build that ENDS on the word (d = build length, 1-4 s): before a reveal, an impact or a silence

reverse_swell.desc: a reversed swell that ENDS on the word: sucks into a cut, a title, a big number

impact.desc: a big cinematic hit with a tail: the act's biggest reveal (at most 1-2 per act)

boom.desc: a deep sub boom: a heavy number lands, a chapter title

sub_drop.desc: a falling sub tone: a crash, a price falling, the floor giving way

braam.desc: a dark low brass blast: menace, a threat revealed

tension.desc: a low suspense drone under a passage (d = length, 3-15 s)

transition.desc: a big whoosh that PEAKS on the cut: a scene change, a camera jump

swoosh.desc: a fast bright swoosh that PEAKS on the word: text or a card flying in

record_scratch.desc: a record scratch stop: 'wait, what?', a comic reversal
